candidates.attacker_control: The pattern argument is a plain application-supplied String. Public entry points `Torpedo.where(String)`, `Torpedo.condition(String)`, `Torpedo.with(String)` (and the Function<String> variants) return an OnGoingStringCondition whose `like(String)`, `notLike(String)` and `like().any/startsWith/endsWith(String)` methods pass the string unchanged to ConditionBuilder.createLike → new LikeCondition(…) → the concatenating createQueryFragment. Typical exercise path: a web search/filter field is passed to like()/startsWith()/endsWith(); a single quote in that value terminates the quoted literal the library emits and the remainder becomes query syntax.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the value is genuinely caller-supplied (String parameters on public interfaces OnGoingStringCondition/OnGoingLikeCondition) and not transformed before use (createLike passes it unmodified). Verified the parameter-binding path used by all sibling predicates (ConditionBuilder eq/neq/lt/lte/gt/gte/in/notIn/between → Selector.generateParameter → ValueParameter `:name` → DefaultQueryBuilder.setParameter), confirming like is an inconsistent raw concatenation rather than the intended parameterization. Verified LikeCondition.getParameters() returns an empty list so no binding can occur; verified no escaping helper exists in the codebase. Considered that the library never itself receives untrusted input — exploitation requires the host application to pass untrusted data to the like API, which is its documented purpose (README example passes literal values to eq; like accepts arbitrary patterns).
candidates.impact: The generated HQL/JPQL predicate is attacker-influenced: a crafted pattern can close the string literal and restructure the WHERE clause (e.g. adding tautologies/OR-ed predicates), which can bypass the caller's intended filter or authorization predicate and expose or act on records outside the intended result set, depending on the host application's query. It also causes functional breakage for legitimate values containing apostrophes. Impact is bounded by the HQL/JPQL grammar implemented by the JPA provider and by how the hosting application executes the query; no runtime exploitation was performed.
candidates.prerequisites: An application built on TorpedoQuery passes an externally influenced string into the like family (like/notLike/any/startsWith/endsWith) and later executes the built Query through an EntityManager. No library-side escaping, whitelisting, or parameter binding is applied anywhere in the repository (searches for quote-escaping/`escape`/`replace("'")` returned no matches), so a value containing a single quote is sufficient.
candidates.root_cause: LikeCondition.createQueryFragment builds the predicate as `selector + " " + getLike() + " '" + type.wrap(toMatch) + "' "` (lines 86-89). Type.wrap (lines 32-58) only prefixes/appends `%` and performs no single-quote escaping, and LikeCondition.getParameters() returns Collections.emptyList() (lines 103-106), so the pattern is never bound as a JPA parameter. In contrast, eq/neq/lt/lte/gt/gte/in/notIn/between all call selector.generateParameter(value), producing a `:name` placeholder (ValueParameter, lines 51-57) that DefaultQueryBuilder.createJPAQuery binds via query.setParameter (lines 430-434). The like value is the sole predicate value interpolated directly into the HQL/JPQL text.
candidates.title: Unescaped `like`/`notLike` pattern concatenated into HQL/JPQL (query injection)
candidates.trace: Torpedo.where(String)/condition(String) (Torpedo.java 624-626, 821-824) → WhereClauseHandler.handle returns a ConditionBuilder (WhereClauseHandler.java 98-105) → ConditionBuilder.like(String)/notLike(String)/any/startsWith/endsWith (ConditionBuilder.java 236-278) → createLike (254-260) → new LikeCondition(selector, toMatch) (LikeCondition.java 79-83) → LikeCondition.createQueryFragment concatenates `... like '<toMatch>'` (86-89) → DefaultQueryBuilder.freezeQuery assembles the full query string (91-113) → createJPAQuery calls entityManager.createQuery(getQuery(...)) (415-416) and only binds the ValueParameters (430-434).
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and the snapshot contains no tests, so runtime exploitation and the exact HQL parser behavior of a downstream provider were not verified. The snapshot contains no downstream callers, so actual attacker reachability depends on the host application's use of like(); HQL/JPQL providers generally do not support stacked statements, so the impact is query-semantics manipulation rather than direct multi-statement execution. The `constant()` and `function(name,...)` raw-fragment APIs are additional unparameterized concatenation points that were not fully traced (rejected as weaker, design-intent leads).
candidates.weakness_type: HQL/JPQL injection - improper neutralization of special elements in a query (CWE-89 / CWE-943)

coverage_summary: Assigned tree contains 122 model-visible source files (all under src/main/java plus pom.xml, README.md, .gitignore, .travis.yml); no test sources are present. The P1 relation index reports complete indexing (122/122 indexed, 0 missing, 0 hash mismatches) with 854 symbols/1529 syntactic edges, which I used only for navigation and then verified against source text. I listed/search-scanned the whole tree and performed line-level reading of the public API surface (Torpedo, TorpedoFunction, OnGoing* interfaces), every query-fragment-producing class (all conditions, functions, handlers, selectors, joins), and the assembly/execution path (DefaultQueryBuilder, QueryBuilder, Where/With configurators); entry-point mapping was confirmed with the index (e.g. ConditionBuilder.like → createLike → LikeCondition.createQueryFragment). Binary-like files are refused by the tools (none relevant here).
limitations: No build, test, or runtime execution was performed; all conclusions are static source inspection and are not runtime-confirmed.
The snapshot has no test sources and no downstream application code, so real attacker reachability depends on how host applications call the like family.
The relation index is syntactic/navigational only (no complete data-flow, reachability, or exploitability proof), and index labels were not treated as verdicts.
HQL/JPQL grammar behavior of specific JPA/Hibernate providers (e.g. whether stacked statements or subqueries are permitted) was not verified.
No git history or patch information was available, so it is unknown whether this snapshot predates or postdates any upstream fix.

Some peripheral files (e.g. Defaults, DoNothingQueryConfigurator, selectors NotSelector/ObjectSelector/SizeSelector, join builder subclasses) were reviewed only via search/listing rather than full line-by-line reading.

rejected_leads.lead: ConstantFunctionHandler / ComparableConstantFunctionHandler return constant.toString() raw into the query fragment (lines 46-48)
rejected_leads.reason: `TorpedoFunction.constant(...)` is an explicit raw-JPQL-constant API intended to embed unquoted literals/expressions; unlike like(), it is not a value-binding comparison API, and abuse requires the developer to deliberately pass attacker data to constant(). Weaker evidence of missing neutralization than the like sink.

rejected_leads.lead: CustomFunctionHandler / TorpedoFunction.function(String name, ...) concatenate a caller-provided function name into `name(%1$s)` (CustomFunctionHandler.java 42-44)
rejected_leads.reason: Documented low-level extension point where the caller supplies the JPQL function identifier itself; no trust-boundary violation inside the library comparable to the like value path.
Class name comes from an actual Class object chosen at compile time via TorpedoFunction.dyn(...), not from an attacker-controlled string; no injection path found.
Operators are hardcoded literals ('+', '-', '*', '/') in MathOperationHandler; not attacker-controlled.

rejected_leads.lead: SubstringFunctionHandler formats beginIndex/endIndex into the function string (line 45)
rejected_leads.reason: Both indexes are Java int primitives; no string injection possible.
Clones the library's own query-builder object graph; no externally supplied serialized data reaches this path in the snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: TorpedoMagic ThreadLocal/static state and MultiClassLoaderProvider adaptive class loading
rejected_leads.reason: Inspecte d but no clear attacker-controlled input or concrete security impact identified; left as an unconfirmed architecture/concurrency observation rather than a finding.

summary: Repository is TorpedoQuery 2.5.3-SNAPSHOT, a Java HQL/JPQL query builder (122 model-visible files, no tests shipped). I traced the query construction and execution pipeline: public builder API (Torpedo.where/condition/with → WhereClauseHandler → ConditionBuilder) → Condition.createQueryFragment implementations → DefaultQueryBuilder.freezeQuery/createJPAQuery. The strongest source-evidenced issue is an HQL/JPQL injection sink in the `like` family: LikeCondition concatenates the caller-supplied pattern as a quoted string literal into the query fragment and never binds it as a parameter, unlike all sibling predicates which use `:name` parameters. Applications that pass untrusted search/filter text to like/notLike/any/startsWith/endsWith can therefore have the query structure altered (CWE-89/CWE-943). Other raw-fragment APIs (`constant()`, `function(name,...)`) were evaluated and rejected as weaker/design-intent leads.
